subject: Exhibit B: 'Shelter' Fee Reset / Anchoring language - markup review
messages:
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@bigfinhealth.com>

Cc: Claire DuPont <claire.dupont@bigfinhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Exhibit B - proposed 'shelter' fee reset language

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for walking through the draft yesterday. Legal here at BigFin reviewed Exhibit B and flagged one item we want to propose as a compromise to our procurement team: a temporary fee reset called a 'Shelter Reset' that activates if usage drops below 40% of the committed minimum for two consecutive quarters. The idea is to avoid double-charging while we migrate workloads to a new region.

We've attached our suggested markup (ExhibitB_pricing_marked.pdf) and a short model showing how the reset would impact fees (pricing-schedule-scenario.xlsx). Conceptually, we propose: 
- A Shelter Reset may be invoked once per 12-month period;
- During Shelter Reset, the monthly minimum reverts to 60% of the contracted minimum for up to 3 months;
- After 3 months, there is a staged ramp-back to the original minimum over the next 2 months;
- No true-up to prior periods (i.e., we would not pay retroactive fees for the months under Shelter Reset).

We understand Redwood's need to preserve economics around capacity planning — happy to take a call to talk through guardrails. Can you confirm whether Redwood would accept a temporary concession like this, and if not, what alternative language you would accept?

Best,
Sofia Ramirez
Senior Procurement Manager
BigFin Health

Sofia — thanks for the clear proposal and the model, appreciated. Looping in Karthik (sales lead) and Laura (contracts) to weigh in. High-level reaction: the Shelter Reset looks reasonable as a customer-first operational remedy, but we need to protect Redwood's capacity and revenue predictability. Two quick flags from my side:

1) Invocation mechanics: we need more precise metrics (what counts as 'usage' and which telemetry is authoritative).
2) Reinstatement economics: a staged ramp is ok, but we will likely need a modest reinstatement surcharge (one-time) to cover reallocation costs if reactivation occurs within 90 days.

Karthik/Laura — can you propose concrete wording that balances BigFin's ask and Redwood's operational constraints? If it's easier, we can offer a single-use Shelter Reset that reduces the minimum to 65% for up to 2 months, with a one-time 10% reinstatement fee applied to the first post-reset invoice. Happy to take a short call to finalize.

Thanks,

Team — quick take from pricing/ops perspective. We should avoid an open-ended operational exposure. Proposed counterlanguage (high level):

1) "Shelter Reset" may be invoked no more than once in a 12-month period and requires 30 days' prior notice, including verification of usage from Redwood's metrics API.
2) During a Shelter Reset, the monthly committed minimum will be reduced to 65% of the then-current committed minimum for two consecutive billing cycles;
3) A one-time reinstatement fee equal to 10% of the first month invoiced after the Reset will apply if usage returns above 75% of committed minimum within 90 days;
4) The Shelter Reset does not change historical invoicing; no retroactive true-ups except for corrective billing errors.

Operationally this gives us predictability while offering BigFin a meaningful one-time concession. If legal wants to soften wording we can provide alternatives. Laura — can you work language into Exhibit B with clear definitions for "usage" (recommend: production tokens measured at the account ID level, averaged daily over the calendar month) and an API endpoint reference?

-Karthik

Hi Sofia / Jasmine,

Thanks — I drafted a precise clause below that aligns with Karthik's proposal and includes a telemetry anchor. Please see the suggested insertion for Exhibit B, which we can incorporate as a short paragraph under "Minimum Commitment Adjustments":

"Shelter Reset Clause (suggested language): 

In the event Customer's measured Production Usage across the Account falls below forty percent (40%) of the Monthly Committed Minimum for two (2) consecutive calendar quarters, Customer may request a Shelter Reset. A Shelter Reset may be requested not more than once in any twelve (12) month period and is effective thirty (30) days after Customer's request, subject to Redwood's verification. During the Shelter Reset period the Monthly Committed Minimum will be reduced to sixty-five percent (65%) of the then-applicable Monthly Committed Minimum for a period of up to two (2) consecutive billing cycles. If Customer's Production Usage increases to at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the then-applicable Monthly Committed Minimum within ninety (90) days following the end of the Shelter Reset period, Customer shall pay a one-time reinstatement fee equal to ten percent (10%) of the invoice for the first post-reset month. "

Definitions / telemetry: "Production Usage" means the total billable token count for requests sent to Redwood's hosted inference endpoint under the Account ID(s) listed in the Order Form, as reported by Redwood's Usage API (https://api.redwood.example.com/usage).

We think this preserves economic certainty and gives BigFin a discrete, measurable relief path. If BigFin prefers slightly longer runway we can offer a 3-month reset with a proportional increase to the reinstatement fee; otherwise we expect this language to be acceptable.

If everyone agrees, Jasmine — can you send this markup back to Sofia (I'll attach a clean Exhibit B PDF with the insertion) and request a short signature cycle so DocuSign can be completed before year-end?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference
